context:
Goal: a CSV re-import refreshes tracking on every device, not only the one that imported.
Problem (risk): the refresh runs on the importing device only and the Worker keeps its stored copy, so a second or fresh device keeps the old tracking value until it imports the same CSV, while a plain overwrite on the Worker would let a stale device revert newer tracking.
Based on (read): the debt record reimport-refresh-stays-on-device: the Worker's sync merge keeps the stored copy, and the refresh does not touch the two-device merge either.
Based on (ruling): your 15 Nov 13:38 CST ruling that a re-import refreshes only the tracking field, on the importing device, and the rule that the saved data's layout never changes.
Departs from: main, where the refresh stays on the importing device — option b adds a refresh map that the Worker applies, and option c adds a per-line tracking stamp.
Waiting on: nothing stopped, since the fix that updates the importing device's own copy is live; the coordinator acts on your pick next.
home: debt reimport-refresh-stays-on-device (lane reimport-tracking-refresh; pull requests 342 and 350 merged 2026-11-16)

lastAnswer.note: None of these: did the coordinator ever act? Message it (saved in git).

options.gain: No change to the Worker and no new risk, and a line on screen never shifts under a stale device.
options.how: You import the CSV on one device. The Worker and the two-device merge stay as they are, and a second or fresh device picks up the new tracking when you import the same CSV there.
options.label: Keep it on the importing device
options.lose: A second or fresh device keeps the old tracking value until it imports the same CSV.
options.note: Ruled out by you (your 2026-11-18 21:54 CST reply: a is definitely out).

options.gain: All your devices follow the refresh without importing the CSV again.
options.how: The importing device sends a list of tracking updates to the Worker, and the Worker applies those updates to its stored copy.
options.label: Send a refresh map with the sync
options.lose: A Worker change and a new merge rule to review, and a stale device could still send an old update.

options.gain: The refresh is safe across all devices, because a stale device cannot revert newer tracking.
options.how: Each line's tracking carries the time it was set, and the newest value wins on every merge, on the Worker and between devices.
options.label: Stamp each line's tracking with a time
options.lose: It changes the saved data's layout, which a standing rule freezes, so it needs your ruling on that rule too.

options.gain: All your devices follow the refresh, a stale CSV cannot put old tracking back over newer tracking, and the saved data's layout does not change.
options.how: The importing device sends a list of tracking updates with the value it saw before. The Worker applies an update only if its stored tracking still equals that old value.
options.label: Send a refresh map, applied only if the Worker's copy is unchanged
options.lose: Not designed or tested yet: the Worker's sync merge changes, and what happens when two devices import at once is unmeasured.

ref: PR 342 (the pull request that refreshes tracking on a re-import); debt reimport-refresh-stays-on-device (the refresh stays on the importing device); item 89 reimport-changed-lines (your ruling that a re-import refreshes tracking only); invariant saved-state-shape (the saved-state shape is fixed)

title: A CSV re-import now refreshes tracking on the device that imports it. Should your other devices get it too?
why: Option c is the one a stale device cannot undo, and it costs your ruling on the saved data's layout; option b is smaller but a stale CSV can revert newer tracking.
